rows.title: GOP super PAC focused on voter registration builds massive organization
rows.standfirst: Engage Texas disclosed Friday that it raised another $2.3 million over the past six months — and that it has also grown to have almost 300 staff members.

rows.title: Texas voter registration deadline is today
rows.standfirst: The last day to register to vote in Texas is Feb. 3.

rows.title: With a month to go, crowded Democratic primary to challenge Cornyn remains full of uncertainty
rows.standfirst: Some of the 12 candidates have clearer advantages than others, but it is an open question who will make a widely expected runoff.

rows.title: Texans, tell us about your experiences with hair discrimination in schools
rows.standfirst: Have you encountered hair-based discrimination in a Texas public school? Fill out the form below, and we’ll be in touch.

rows.title: Analysis: In 2020’s Texas legislative elections, competition is tricky business
rows.standfirst: Special interest groups and their lobbyists don’t like to campaign against incumbent legislators, for fear they’ll suffer if those incumbents return for another session. That “friendly incumbent” policy has spread to lawmakers themselves.

rows.title: 5 takeaways from the latest congressional fundraising reports
rows.standfirst: The filings were due Friday and shed new light on Texas’ massive U.S. House battlefield, which includes seven Democrat-targeted seats, six open seats, two Republican-targeted seats and a couple of serious primary challenges.

rows.title: Hegar gets heavy outside support in crowded Democratic primary to challenge Cornyn
rows.standfirst: A pro-Hegar group, VoteVets, is launching a $3.3 million TV ad buy backing her as she tries to make it to an all-but-guaranteed runoff.

rows.title: Austin’s homeless residents consider Abbott’s camp helpful but say his tweets still stigmatize them
rows.standfirst: As the governor latches on to violent incidents to criticize Austin city leaders, people experiencing homelessness say he’s painting them with too broad of a brush.

rows.title: Texas freshman Rep. Veronica Escobar boosts national profile with State of the Union response in Spanish
rows.standfirst: Escobar said she plans to highlight health care, immigration, climate change and impeachment in her speech Tuesday night.

rows.title: Here’s how Texas Democrats dole out their 261 delegates in the presidential primary
rows.standfirst: Some delegates are selected statewide, others are determined within state Senate districts and others go to members of Congress or national committee members, who can vote for the candidate of their choice.

rows.title: Connecting Texas: Roads and bridges connect us
rows.standfirst: Roads are about destinations. They’re also about destiny.

rows.title: Analysis: Cornyn’s expected vote against impeachment is in tune with Republican voters in Texas
rows.standfirst: Whatever the reason is for U.S. Sen. John Cornyn’s support for the president, it puts him tightly in sync with Republican voters in Texas.

rows.title: Analysis: A Texas sales tax rule hinges on a question: What’s local?
rows.standfirst: This is the kind of question that makes tax consultants wealthy: If a Texan buys something online, should the local sales tax go to the seller’s city or the buyer’s?

rows.title: Texas A&M-Commerce calls shooting incident “targeted, isolated,” identifies victims
rows.standfirst: The university confirmed three gunshot victims at a residence hall on campus. There are two confirmed deaths. A toddler at the scene was taken to the hospital for treatment.

rows.title: Outside money floods Cuellar primary, with U.S. Chamber of Commerce latest to join the fray
rows.standfirst: The Republican-leaning business group went on TV on Tuesday in the nationally watched primary, which has drawn over $2 million in outside spending.

rows.title: Partisan tension hung over State of the Union — even before Texas congresswoman gave rebuttal from El Paso
rows.standfirst: President Donald Trump touted economic and military successes. U.S. Rep. Lloyd Doggett of Austin was among Democrats who walked out. Afterwards, U.S. Rep. Veronica Escobar rebutted Trump’s speech from El Paso.

rows.title: Texas Southern University regents vote to fire school’s president
rows.standfirst: President Austin Lane was suspended in mid-January from the top post at the historically black school in Houston with little explanation. Now regents have voted to terminate him over allegations of admissions irregularities and other contract violations.

rows.title: Michael Bloomberg is opening 11 additional field offices in Texas ahead of Super Tuesday
rows.standfirst: The campaign initially made its ambitious plans known late last year when it named its first four hires here, including a state director.

rows.title: New Texas election process has Democrats expecting a delay in Super Tuesday delegate totals
rows.standfirst: Democratic leaders say the Texas secretary of state’s office told them that a full accounting of how many delegates each presidential contender wins won’t be available on election night. But the secretary of state’s office says it does plan to have the results tabulated.

rows.title: TribCast: Forecasting a Super Tuesday delay in Texas and the upcoming primary
rows.standfirst: On this week’s TribCast, Alexa talks to Matthew, Patrick and Ross about an expected delay in Super Tuesday delegate totals in Texas and what we’re keeping an eye on for the upcoming primaries.

rows.title: Ted Cruz and John Cornyn join successful effort to acquit President Donald Trump
rows.standfirst: Both Texas Republicans voted not to convict on charges of abuse of power and obstruction of Congress.

rows.title: The on-air authority on state politics and policy
rows.standfirst: More than a website, The Texas Tribune has worked to grow its reach and foster an engaged electorate by appearing on television news stations across the state.

rows.title: Report: Six Texas oil refineries spewing cancer-causing pollutant above federal threshold
rows.standfirst: An environmental nonprofit has released an analysis of first-of-its-kind air monitoring data that shows benzene levels at 10 U.S. petroleum refineries exceeded limits established in an Obama-era environmental regulation. Six are in Texas.

rows.title: Texas executes Abel Ochoa, who killed five family members in Dallas shooting
rows.standfirst: Ochoa was sentenced to death after the slayings in Dallas of his relatives, including his two young daughters. His defense argued he was in a cocaine-induced delirium.

rows.title: El Paso shooting suspect faces nearly 100 federal charges, including hate crimes
rows.standfirst: Patrick Crusius, the alleged gunman in the Aug. 3 massacre at a Walmart store, already faces state capital murder charges for the racially motivated shooting spree that also wounded dozens.

rows.title: After black student suspended over dreadlocks, some Texas lawmakers want to ban hair discrimination
rows.standfirst: The Texas Legislative Black Caucus hopes to pass the CROWN Act in the next legislative session. The bill would prohibit hair discrimination affecting people of color in schools and workplaces.

rows.title: “Neglected” college campuses on Texas border want a little love, and better Wi-Fi
rows.standfirst: At three lonely satellite campuses of Sul Ross State University, students and teachers say they’re stuck with broken technology and few resources. Their dreams of blooming into an independent four-year university seem doomed, but they hope things might get better under a new university president.

rows.title: Three Texas inmates have died at the hands of prison officers as use of force continues to rise
rows.standfirst: The increase in altercations with inmates comes as Texas’ prison population dwindles. In three years, three officers have faced criminal charges in prisoners’ deaths.

rows.title: Analysis: Messing with elections messes with democracy
rows.standfirst: Voter suppression, incompetent administrators, dirty political tricks, and misinformation and political rhetoric attacking the results of elections present threats to elections and democracy, a new book argues. It came out on the day of the Iowa caucuses.

rows.title: U.S. Rep. Bill Flores makes endorsement in crowded Republican primary to succeed him
rows.standfirst: The retiring Bryan Republican is backing Waco business owner Renee Swann in the 11-way primary.

rows.title: Cristina Tzintzún Ramirez’s unlikely ally in her quest to take on John Cornyn: Alec Baldwin
rows.standfirst: In Baldwin, most recently known for his recurring portrayal of President Donald Trump on ”Saturday Night Live,” Tzintzún Ramirez has found a generous financial supporter and an informal adviser.

rows.title: Analysis: The politics of paying one Texan’s local sales taxes to another Texan’s city
rows.standfirst: A longstanding economic development incentive tied to local sales taxes has run into a hurdle, as voters find out some of their local dollars are ending up in faraway localities. Blame the internet.

rows.title: Texas asks U.S. Supreme Court to end California law banning state-funded travel
rows.standfirst: After Texas passed a law in 2017 allowing foster care agencies to cite sincerely held religious beliefs to deny placements to gay couples, California banned state-funded travel to the Lone Star State.

rows.title: Amanda Edwards lost a family member to gun violence. But she doesn’t want to “take your AR-15.”
rows.standfirst: The U.S. Senate candidate’s proposals on guns and other issues are moderate compared with those of some of her primary competitors — but she said they have the most realistic chance of passing.

rows.title: Beto O’Rourke’s flock remains loyal while his party debates whether to move on
rows.standfirst: The question facing Texas Democrats: Can the party capitalize on the energy he brings out of his supporters while minimizing the counter-energy he seems to provoke from the right?

rows.title: Texas updates election reporting system to allow for tally of Super Tuesday delegates
rows.standfirst: After Democrats raised the prospect of delays in calculating presidential delegates on election night, the secretary of state’s office has updated the system counties will use to report results on March 3.

rows.title: To end hazing, students must be individually punished or prosecuted, advocates tell Texas lawmakers
rows.standfirst: Legislation passed last year increases university transparency and strengthens the state’s definition of hazing. But advocates say when it comes to enforcement, kicking fraternities off campus isn’t enough.

rows.title: How are the top Democratic U.S. Senate candidates in Texas different? We asked them 11 questions to find out.
rows.standfirst: To help voters make sense of the U.S. Senate race, we asked the top candidates in the 2020 Democratic primary a series of simple questions designed to help voters understand their political and policy-based differences.

rows.title: Chris Bell has been running for office for decades. Is he the Democrat to take on John Cornyn?
rows.standfirst: Bell is the only candidate running in the U.S. Senate Democratic primary who has experience in Washington, D.C. But he has more experience running campaigns than winning them.

rows.title: T-Squared: This is your 2020 Texas Tribune Festival save-the-date
rows.standfirst: Our 10th annual ideas weekend will be Sept. 24-26 — once again in downtown Austin, in the shadow of the Capitol. We’ll talk about the momentous election cycle; the coming legislative session; big issues like school finance, renewable energy and criminal justice reform; and so much more.

rows.title: TribCast: Texas Democrats’ Beto O’Rourke dilemma and the road to Super Tuesday
rows.standfirst: On this week’s TribCast, Alexa talks to Matthew, Ross and Alex about the questions facing Texas Democrats on how much of a role they want O’Rourke to play in their elections and the setup for Super Tuesday voting in the state.

rows.title: Leader of Texas’ health department leaving after a year for Louisiana job
rows.standfirst: Courtney Phillips is leaving the state Health and Human Services Commission to take a job as Louisiana’s new secretary of the Department of Health.

rows.title: Trump endorses in three competitive Texas congressional primary races
rows.standfirst: The president gave his backing to three candidates who have been leading their primary races but are trying to avoid runoffs in crowded fields.

rows.title: T-Squared: The Texas Tribune’s 2020 diversity report
rows.standfirst: We’ve made progress, but there’s more work we can do to ensure our newsroom resembles Texas — and our journalism is as good as it can be.

rows.title: Royce West helped flip Dallas County for Democrats in 2006. Could he flip Texas in 2020?
rows.standfirst: In a crowded Democratic field to challenge U.S. Sen. John Cornyn, the longtime state senator is betting on his decades of experience as a consensus builder.

rows.title: Our updated Texas 2020 Hotlist: The most competitive races in this year’s primary
rows.standfirst: A couple of The Texas Tribune’s political nerds highlight (their latest version of) the most interesting races up and down the 2020 primary ballot.

rows.title: Texas improperly picked winners for contracts worth $10 billion, health insurers argue
rows.standfirst: More than half a dozen health plans are appealing the contract decisions for STAR+PLUS, the state’s privatized insurance program for elderly, blind and disabled Texans.

rows.title: After strong finishes in Iowa and New Hampshire, Pete Buttigieg turns to Texas
rows.standfirst: Starting Monday, the campaign will have 24 paid staffers in the state of Texas, which holds its primary March 3.

rows.title: Houston Mayor Sylvester Turner said Mike Bloomberg’s apology for “stop and frisk” was key to endorsement
rows.standfirst: Turner’s endorsement comes amid controversy over Bloomberg’s “stop and frisk” policy during his time as mayor of New York City.

rows.title: First case of coronavirus identified in Texas; group returning from China quarantined in San Antonio
rows.standfirst: The patient is among a group of people who returned from Hubei Province, China, and are under federal quarantine at a military base in San Antonio.

rows.title: Greg Abbott plans pre-primary tour supporting GOP state House incumbents, candidates
rows.standfirst: The governor is hitting the campaign trail for at least 10 House incumbents and candidates whom he has endorsed.

rows.title: Pentagon to divert $3.8 billion from its budget to build more of Trump’s border barrier
rows.standfirst: Money that had been earmarked to buy military aircraft will instead be used for President Donald Trump’s promised border wall.

rows.title: Hearing airs sexual abuse claims against KIPP charter school co-founder Mike Feinberg
rows.standfirst: An administrative hearing into whether Mike Feinberg can keep his Texas educator certificate turned into a de facto trial over the sexual abuse allegation that led to his dismissal from the charter network he co-founded in the 1990s.

rows.title: Diversion of aircraft purchases for border wall puts some Texas Republicans in a difficult position
rows.standfirst: Military aircraft construction is vital to the Fort Worth economy. The diversion drew condemnation from Democrats and at least one Texas Republican.

rows.title: T-Squared: Meet our new Houston reporter and our new audience analyst
rows.standfirst: Mitchell Ferman joins The Texas Tribune in March as our first Houston-based reporter, covering energy and the economy. Jon Garza is the latest addition to our audience team.

rows.title: Claims of carpetbagging fly in Texas congressional primary
rows.standfirst: Candidates across the state are being accused of “district shopping” as opponents question their ties to the places they want to represent. The dynamic is playing out mostly in GOP primaries and particularly in more rural districts.

rows.title: MJ Hegar says her military experience makes her the fighter Democrats need to take on John Cornyn
rows.standfirst: Hegar is best known for her heroism on the battlefield when she co-piloted a helicopter that was shot down by the Taliban. But her experience also includes other challenges she faced as a woman serving her country.

rows.title: Bernie Sanders leaps to first among Texas Democrats in latest UT/TT Poll
rows.standfirst: Sanders now leads the Democratic presidential candidates among Texas voters, but Donald Trump maintains a slight lead over each of the top Democrats in the race, according to the latest University of Texas/Texas Tribune Poll.

rows.title: Impeachment left Texas voters sour on the president and both parties in Congress, UT/TT Poll finds
rows.standfirst: Texas voters give low marks to the leaders involved in impeachment proceedings, showing their partisan stripes in their assessments, according to the latest University of Texas/Texas Tribune Poll.

rows.title: Judge calls opponent “selfish” for wanting to “break barriers” as first elected female chief justice of Texas Supreme Court
rows.standfirst: Jerry Zimmerer, an appellate judge in Houston, said his campaign differs from Amy Clark Meachum’s because “I actually want the best candidate to win.”

rows.title: Julián Castro endorses Jessica Cisneros, the candidate challenging U.S. Rep. Henry Cuellar
rows.standfirst: Castro, whose brother serves with Cuellar in Congress, is backing Jessica Cisneros.

rows.title: Trump administration taps elite Border Patrol units to arrest immigrants inside the United States
rows.standfirst: Houston is among the U.S. cities where highly trained teams will embed with Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents.

rows.title: Clayton Williams, oilman and colorful candidate for Texas governor, has died
rows.standfirst: Williams, a well-known oilman and entrepreneur from Midland, has died. The one-time Republican candidate for governor of Texas lost a nationally watched race against Democrat Ann Richards in 1990 after a series of public gaffes.

rows.title: Ted Cruz, once a Trump rival, worked to save his presidency
rows.standfirst: Cruz, a U.S. senator from Texas, once called Trump “utterly amoral” and a “sniveling coward.” Then he worked to save his presidency.

rows.title: Political Pick’em: Can you guess who will win these Texas primaries?
rows.standfirst: The Texas Tribune is excited to present a return of its Political Pick’em contest. We’ve selected a handful of competitive Texas primaries, and we want you to pick the candidates who you think will get the most votes.

rows.title: The billionaire Wilks family bankrolls one of its own in run for Texas House
rows.standfirst: The family has pumped millions from its fracking fortune into Texas politics, backing hardline conservative candidates and causes. Now one member of the clan is vying for the House District 60 seat being vacated by Rep. Mike Lang.

rows.title: MJ Hegar leads the Democratic U.S. Senate candidates, UT/TT Poll finds
rows.standfirst: Hegar leads a crowded field of Democrats running for the seat held by U.S. Sen. John Cornyn, according to the latest University of Texas/Texas Tribune Poll.

rows.title: Most Texans want lower property taxes and more school spending, UT/TT Poll finds
rows.standfirst: It’s not a new contradiction, but it’s persistent: Texas voters think that property taxes are too high and that school spending is too low, according to the latest University of Texas/Texas Tribune Poll.

rows.title: U.S. citizens exposed to coronavirus on cruise ship quarantined in Texas and California
rows.standfirst: More than a dozen Americans who tested positive for coronavirus have been quarantined at military bases in the two states, federal officials said Monday.

rows.title: Early voting is underway in Texas. Here’s what you need to know.
rows.standfirst: Early voting will last for 10 days, ending Feb. 28. The primary is March 3.

rows.title: Watch the U.S. Senate Democratic primary debate
rows.standfirst: Eleven of the Democratic candidates running to challenge Republican U.S. Sen. John Cornyn will debate onstage starting at 6:30 p.m. Tuesday.

rows.title: Support for background checks on all gun sales remains high, UT/TT Poll finds
rows.standfirst: Texans are divided about whether more people carrying guns would make the U.S. safer, but a large majority favors expanding mental health and criminal background checks on gun sales, according to the latest University of Texas/Texas Tribune Poll.

rows.title: Border issues still loom in Texas voters’ views, UT/TT Poll finds
rows.standfirst: Border security and immigration continue to dominate Texas voters’ thoughts about the most important problems facing the state, according to the latest University of Texas/Texas Tribune Poll.

rows.title: Presidential candidates turn their focus to Texas as early voting begins
rows.standfirst: Early voting in Texas starts Tuesday, ahead of the headline-grabbing election days in Nevada and South Carolina. As a result, the state is getting a lot of attention from the Democrats running for president.

rows.title: Joaquin Castro endorses Cristina Tzintzún Ramirez in crowded primary to challenge John Cornyn
rows.standfirst: The endorsement is among the biggest yet in the 12-way primary, and it comes as early voting begins Tuesday.

rows.title: State Sen. Kirk Watson to retire from Texas Senate
rows.standfirst: Watson has represented Austin in the Texas Senate since 2007.

rows.title: Texas public education poll is an asset for all
rows.standfirst: For many years, the Raise Your Hand Texas Foundation, along with numerous friends and colleagues, has worked tirelessly on programs and policies aimed at strengthening and improving public education in our state. When we took a step back, however, we realized that while we are certainly affecting and supporting public education, we haven’t been tracking the impact of our work as reflected in the attitudes and opinions of Texans over time.

rows.title: During debate, Texas Democratic U.S. Senate candidates differ on best way to oust Republican John Cornyn
rows.standfirst: Eleven of the 12 people seeking the Democratic nomination for the 2020 U.S. Senate race in Texas faced off in a debate Tuesday. It’s been decades since someone from the party represented the state in the upper chamber.

rows.title: Tenth Talks: Watch three experts predict the future of higher education in Texas
rows.standfirst: In this edition of Tenth Talks, a Texas Tribune video series on the next 10 years of Texas, three of the state’s top higher education leaders and innovators predict what’s in store for their field.

rows.title: Most Texas voters — but not most Republicans — would admit refugees from other countries, UT/TT Poll finds
rows.standfirst: While most Texas voters would welcome refugees into the state, fewer than a third of Republican voters agree, according to the latest University of Texas/Texas Tribune Poll.

rows.title: Cristina Tzintzún Ramirez gets super PAC help in Democratic primary to challenge Cornyn
rows.standfirst: A new group, Lone Star Forward, is beginning a TV ad buy Wednesday boosting Tzintzún Ramirez as she looks to qualify for a likely runoff for the Democratic nomination for Senate.

rows.title: Federal judge dismisses suit against Army Corps for post-Harvey flooding
rows.standfirst: U.S. Judge Loren A. Smith threw out a case brought by Houstonians whose properties flooded as a result of releases from Addicks and Barker dams.

rows.title: TribCast: A Texas Senate retirement and Bernie Sanders’ new lead in the state
rows.standfirst: On this week’s TribCast, Alexa talks to Emma, Cassi and Alex about what state Sen. Kirk Watson’s retirement could mean for the Senate, Bernie Sanders’ new lead in presidential polling in Texas and a Democratic judicial candidate’s sexist comments about his opponent.

rows.title: Republican congressional candidate Jamie Berryhill compares borderless nation to a woman “raped and defiled”
rows.standfirst: The Facebook post has since been deleted. Berryhill told a local TV station he wouldn’t make similar comments again.

rows.title: TribCast, special edition: Our pollsters analyze the latest UT/TT Poll on primary races and issues in Texas
rows.standfirst: In this edition of the TribCast, Ross talks to pollsters Joshua Blank, James Henson and Daron Shaw about the latest University of Texas/Texas Tribune Poll, the state’s presidential and Senate primaries, and what Texas voters said about issues facing the state.

rows.title: Democrats think campaigning on health care will flip an Austin-area U.S. House seat. But will the nominee also need star power?
rows.standfirst: In a district with no clear frontrunner for the Democratic nomination, the party is looking to re-create MJ Hegar’s momentum — and hopes focusing on issues will flip the seat.

rows.title: In Democrats’ low-information judicial primaries, gender and ballot names may drive voters’ decisions
rows.standfirst: Fourteen Democrats are competing for seven seats on the Texas Supreme Court and Court of Criminal Appeals. How do you win when no one knows your name?

rows.title: Texas anti-abortion activists take on baby Tinslee’s life support case, attempting to strike down a law that protects doctors
rows.standfirst: An anti-abortion group and conservative elected officials have framed Tinslee Lewis’ case as a “right to life” issue. But medical experts say continuing care is hurting the baby and doctors need protections to make these kinds of decisions.

rows.title: As the Texas prison population shrinks, the state is closing two more lockups
rows.standfirst: The closures are expected in the coming months, as the state faces dangerous understaffing in its prisons.

rows.title: Texas Southern University and ousted president agree to part ways
rows.standfirst: Regents had accused President Austin Lane of failing to report allegations of fraud in the university admissions process and other contract violations. Their agreement to end his tenure contains no claims of wrongdoing.

rows.title: Coronavirus quarantine in San Antonio ends for 90 evacuees from China
rows.standfirst: Those being released from quarantine “pose no health risk to the surrounding community, or to the communities they will be returning to,” according to the Centers for Disease Control.

rows.title: Lewd tweets, the N-word and just plain weirdness: A wild-card candidate rattles education board races.
rows.standfirst: Eight seats are in play for the 15-member State Board of Education, which decides what Texas children are taught. Democrats hope to pick up seats in November, but for now, both parties just want to see Robert Morrow lose his GOP primary.

rows.title: Democrat Mike Siegel’s close loss in 2018 won him tougher primary competition this year for a nationally targeted congressional seat
rows.standfirst: The Austin lawyer said the party left the 10th District for dead until he came within 5 points of winning in 2018. Now, Siegel is up against two new challengers who say he can’t finish the job.

rows.title: Abbott-backed candidate fights Schofield for his old seat as November looms large
rows.standfirst: After narrowly losing reelection in 2018, former state Rep. Mike Schofield is making a comeback bid — against a Republican primary newcomer endorsed by Gov. Greg Abbott.

rows.title: Analysis: Is Texas political sentiment changing?
rows.standfirst: The 2020 elections are a test of whether Democratic hopes and Republican fears — borne of the close finishes in the 2018 elections — are justified. The UT/TT Poll results on that question offer some clues.

rows.title: MJ Hegar keeps fundraising lead as Democratic primary to challenge Cornyn reaches end
rows.standfirst: In the crowded field of U.S. Senate candidates, Hegar raised $638,000 during the first six weeks of 2020, according to campaign finance reports that were due Thursday.

rows.title: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez endorses Cristina Tzintzún Ramirez in Democratic primary to challenge Cornyn
rows.standfirst: The endorsement comes less than two weeks before a primary that is almost certain to go to a runoff.

rows.title: Texas coronavirus cases climb to three after two cruise ship evacuees are diagnosed
rows.standfirst: More than 300 Americans on the cruise ship were repatriated Monday. Of those, 18 have been confirmed to have coronavirus, including two being held at a San Antonio military base, the Centers of Disease Control and Prevention said.

rows.title: Sanders cranks up Texas primary push with early voting underway
rows.standfirst: The Democratic presidential candidate is hosting four rallies in the state this weekend and bulking up his staff here.

rows.title: Texas sues company whose Port Neches chemical plant exploded
rows.standfirst: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton sued TPC Group on Friday, citing a slew of environmental violations at its Port Neches facility, including ones connected to a Nov. 27 explosion.

rows.title: Nancy Pelosi gives Henry Cuellar a homestretch boost in intense primary, calling for “resounding victory”
rows.standfirst: During a trip to Laredo on Saturday, the U.S. House speaker swung by a Cuellar campaign office with 10 days until the Texas primary.

rows.title: A confident Bernie Sanders barnstorms Texas with burst of momentum
rows.standfirst: The Democratic presidential candidate swung through Texas this weekend as he enjoyed a resounding victory in the Nevada caucuses and eyes another big win March 3.

rows.title: Hemp is booming in Texas. Distinguishing it from marijuana is still a challenge.
rows.standfirst: In this video, The Texas Tribune dug into hemp and marijuana with lawmakers, crime lab scientists, criminal defense attorneys and hemp entrepreneurs.

rows.title: How are Texas public schools engaging with the 2020 presidential election? Share your story.
rows.standfirst: At a divisive and dramatic moment in U.S. politics, we’d like students and teachers to tell us what they’re learning, talking about and missing as they follow the presidential race.

rows.title: Analysis: Why would a Texas Democrat want a seat in the Republican state Senate?
rows.standfirst: On paper, Texas senators have it better than their counterparts in the Texas House, but why would a Democrat want to work in a place where Republicans are fully and completely in control?

rows.title: Analysis: Health care and its discontents loom over Texas Democrats in 2020
rows.standfirst: Texas Democrats, like Democrats elsewhere, put health care at or near the top of their lists of most important problems. But they have significant disagreements among themselves over what to do about it.

rows.title: Speaking statistically, this GOP donor wants to convince you that money buys justice in Texas
rows.standfirst: After losing a case at the all-Republican Texas Supreme Court, millionaire Salem Abraham set out to mathematically test the idea that campaign contributions influence the elected justices. Now he wants to change the system.

rows.title: Former UT coach Michael Center sentenced to six months in connection with admissions scandal
rows.standfirst: Center took a $100,000 bribe in exchange for marking a prospective student a tennis recruit. The student had no background in tennis and left the team shortly after being accepted into the university.

rows.title: State Sen. Eddie Lucio Jr. bets on experience, seniority as he confronts two Democratic primary challengers
rows.standfirst: The longtime state senator from Brownsville is hoping his upper-chamber clout can ward off two intraparty opponents questioning his Democratic credentials.

rows.title: To fight huge drop in bus riders, North Texas transit agency faces hard choices about who gets service
rows.standfirst: The new bus layout coming in 2022 might bring more service to high-demand areas, but it could also modify routes that serve people at their doorsteps.

rows.title: Webb County and Laredo coming face to face with the reality of a border wall
rows.standfirst: Webb County hasn’t seen the buildup of barriers that El Paso or the Rio Grande Valley has since 2006. But change is coming, and it’s coming quickly.

rows.title: Baylor University celebrates 175 years
rows.standfirst: On February 1, the Baylor Family celebrated the achievement of a remarkable milestone of leadership and service to our state and nation. On that day 175 years ago, the Republic of Texas chartered Baylor University. As we observe this anniversary, Baylor proudly stands as the oldest continuously operating university in the State of Texas.

rows.title: “It’s a joke”: Flaring expert finds big problems in report from Texas oil and gas regulator
rows.standfirst: “It looks more like a political manifesto to me,” a Texas A&M professor said about a report from the Railroad Commission of Texas.

rows.title: After penalizing gay teacher, Mansfield ISD awards her $100,000, plans vote to ban sexual orientation discrimination
rows.standfirst: As part of the settlement, the school district agreed to provide mandatory training to human resources and counseling staff on LGBTQ issues in schools, and to require its board of trustees to vote on whether to add protections for sexual orientation into its policies.

rows.title: Bernie Sanders stokes question for Texas Democrats: How would his nomination affect their down-ballot plans?
rows.standfirst: Sanders supporters say he’ll bring new voters to the polls to help Democrats flip Texas, but some establishment figures are in panic mode.

rows.title: ACLU sues seven Texas towns for passing local anti-abortion ordinances
rows.standfirst: The lawsuit takes aim at towns that have declared themselves “sanctuary cities for the unborn.”

rows.title: T-Squared: Take The Texas Tribune’s annual reader survey
rows.standfirst: Your responses will help us better understand the people consuming our journalism and how they use it — and that will make us better equipped to serve you.

rows.title: More young Texans are registering to vote. Will they actually turn out?
rows.standfirst: Voter registration activity at Texas high schools spiked ahead of the 2018 general elections, when young and Hispanic voters turned out in record numbers for a midterm.

rows.title: With an unusually large Democratic field on Super Tuesday, delegate cutoff looms large for some presidential candidates in Texas
rows.standfirst: Recent polls suggest some candidates could miss the threshold to collect statewide delegates. That includes Michael Bloomberg, who has put more effort into the state than any other primary candidate.

rows.title: This judge refused to toss Rick Perry’s indictment. Now Perry is backing his opponent in Court of Criminal Appeals race.
rows.standfirst: A PAC with close ties to Perry is backing Gina Parker’s campaign to oust incumbent Judge Bert Richardson in the GOP primary.

rows.title: Analysis: The Texas Supreme Court and the ruling class
rows.standfirst: A well-heeled loser of a lawsuit that went to the Texas Supreme Court did a detailed analysis and concluded that the big law firms that politically support the judges get the best results. Maybe money is the reason, maybe it’s not.

rows.title: U.S. Rep. Louie Gohmert of Texas one of four House members to vote against anti-lynching bill
rows.standfirst: Gohmert said he voted against the legislation because the penalty was not harsh enough.

rows.title: TribCast: Bernie Sanders’ Super Tuesday momentum and judicial election questions
rows.standfirst: On this week’s TribCast, Alexa talks to Matthew, Patrick and Emma about Bernie Sanders’ momentum going into Super Tuesday, how that’s stoking concerns among some Democrats and the questions that come with judicial elections.

rows.title: Texas state crime labs won’t test suspected marijuana in low-level cases
rows.standfirst: The Texas Department of Public Safety said last week that it would not perform testing to distinguish between hemp and marijuana in misdemeanor cases.

rows.title: Ask us anything: Three political reporters will answer your questions about the Texas primary
rows.standfirst: Join us Monday in r/politics on Reddit to ask journalists from The Texas Tribune, Texas Observer and Texas Monthly anything about the upcoming primary election.

rows.title: Abbott says the homeless need mental health care. Advocates say Medicaid expansion would help.
rows.standfirst: Abbott has long opposed extending state-funded health coverage to 1.5 million Texans under the Affordable Care Act. But a spokesman for the governor did not rule out a possible coverage expansion under a new Trump administration block grant policy.

rows.title: Baylor University, a legacy of leaders and servants in Texas
rows.standfirst: Founded by the Republic of Texas on February 1, 1845, Baylor University is celebrating its 175th anniversary. Baylor’s impact on the surrounding world can be measured in several ways; one of the most distinctive is the number of leaders who, following their education at Baylor, went on to assume prominent roles in their professions and communities.

rows.title: T-Squared: Meet five star reporters on the ProPublica/Texas Tribune investigative team
rows.standfirst: In the first wave of hires for our ambitious investigative partnership, we’ve added five standout reporters who are smart, authentic and fearless truth-tellers.

rows.title: Democratic presidential candidates begin to crowd Texas for final pre-primary sprint
rows.standfirst: Most candidates are traveling to Texas — some of them twice — ahead of the state’s delegate-rich primary Tuesday.

rows.title: FBI agents investigating Houston ISD offices
rows.standfirst: It’s unclear why the FBI showed up at the Hattie Mae White Educational Support Center and the home of a district official, but Houston ISD said there is no danger to students, staff or the community.

rows.title: Abbott’s state-run camp for the homeless in Austin to be taken over by nonprofit with new shelter plans
rows.standfirst: The Texas Department of Transportation will begin lease negotiations with ATX Helps, which plans to construct a large shelter on the southeast Austin property where more than 100 people reside. Some camp residents say they’re concerned about the proposed changes.

rows.title: Water main rupture sets off major disruption in Houston: citywide boil notice, Loop 610 flooded
rows.standfirst: The main break caused some early voting locations to close. All Houston ISD schools were closed Friday and set to reopen Monday, the school district announced.

rows.title: Joe Biden has long held a lead with black voters in Texas. Will they stick with him?
rows.standfirst: Many black voters in the Lone Star State and elsewhere are wondering aloud whether to look elsewhere. If they do, his campaign could be in trouble.

rows.title: Analysis: Final pitches mark the end of the 2020 Texas primaries
rows.standfirst: You can tell by the number of visits from presidential candidates that the state is getting in the next few days: Election day is almost here.

rows.title: Two Texas House Republicans battle right flank in otherwise calm primary season
rows.standfirst: GOP state Reps. J.D. Sheffield of Gatesville and Dan Flynn of Canton are standing out as perhaps the most vulnerable House Republicans days out from the primary election.

rows.title: Texas is an open primary state. Here’s what that means for how Republicans, Democrats and others can vote on Super Tuesday.
rows.standfirst: Texas is one of 17 states with open primaries, which means regardless of which party voters identify with, they can choose from year to year which party’s nominees they’d like to select in a primary election.

rows.title: President Trump’s “remain in Mexico” policy blocked in federal court
rows.standfirst: The program, officially known as the Migrant Protection Protocols, called for pushing asylum seekers back into Mexico to await their U.S. hearings. It aimed to curb migration across the U.S. southern border.

rows.title: Texas Republicans raise alarms about coronavirus threat at the southern border
rows.standfirst: The lawmakers concede there is no major present-day outbreak of the deadly strain in Mexico, South America or Central America but note that “it can be presumed that we will see the virus spread further.”

rows.title: T-Squared: We’ve hired Stacy-Marie Ishmael and Millie Tran to lead us in our second decade
rows.standfirst: These superlative journalists and inspiring role models will be The Texas Tribune’s new editorial director and chief product officer, respectively. We’re so lucky to have them on our team.

rows.title: Donald Trump to nominate U.S. Rep. John Ratcliffe to become director of national intelligence
rows.standfirst: Ratcliffe was previously considered for the role but withdrew his name after he was accused of exaggerating parts of his biography, like his role as the leader of an immigration crackdown while he was a federal prosecutor in the Eastern District of Texas.

rows.title: In two Texas prisoner deaths, one former officer is indicted after another’s case is cleared
rows.standfirst: A former correctional officer was charged with aggravated assault by a public servant Thursday in Walker County, a week after another man was cleared of criminal charges in another inmate homicide.

rows.title: Dueling “remain in Mexico” orders cause confusion and tension in the borderlands
rows.standfirst: The temporary closing of the Paso Del Norte international bridge capped off a day of confusion and chaos after a federal appellate court blocked the Migrant Protection Protocols.

rows.title: Early voting is over. Here’s what turnout looked like in Texas’ 10 biggest counties.
rows.standfirst: Turnout was higher than in 2016 among Democrats, and lower among Republicans.
